Proposition
[The Euclidean Distance]

↗ def:riemannian-distance ↗ ex:euclidean-metric

On $\mathbb R^n$ with the Euclidean metric $\bar g$ of Example 2, \[ d_{\bar g}(x,y)=|x-y|, \qquad x,y\in \mathbb R^n. \] This is Definition 15 in the Euclidean case; its real-valued form is Lemma 2.
Proof

↗ def:riemannian-distance ↗ ex:euclidean-metric \sketch The segment $\gamma (t)=x+t(y-x)$ has length $|y-x|$, giving $d_{\bar g}(x,y)\le |x-y|$. For any $C^1$ competitor,

\[ |y-x|=\left|\int _0^1\gamma '(t)\, dt\right|\le \int _0^1|\gamma '(t)|\, dt=L_{\bar g}(\gamma ), \]

so the reverse inequality follows on taking the infimum.

□
